slides.title: Keep ground coffee fresh longer
slides.subtitle: Three simple rules, and the one that matters most.

slides.title: Air is the main enemy
slides.body: Oxygen speeds up staling more than anything else. Ground coffee exposes far more surface to the air than whole beans, so it fades faster.

slides.title: Light dulls the flavor
slides.body: Clear canisters let light in, and that can dull the taste. Pick an opaque container, or keep a clear one inside a closed cupboard.

slides.title: Heat and moisture speed it up
slides.body: Warmth and moisture both make coffee go stale sooner. Skip the cabinet by the oven or dishwasher, and the sunny windowsill.

slides.caption: About how long ground coffee stays at its best at room temperature, in a sealed container.

slides.label: The tip
slides.body: Buy only what you will use in a week or two. A small bag bought often beats a big one that sits.

slides.title: Sealed, dark, cool, and soon
slides.body: Close it tight, keep it dark and cool, and use it within a couple of weeks.
